ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: time and ticks
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Ticks, hours, days, quadrums and years, and how to convert them
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A year on the Rim is only 60 days long, so birthdays come around fast.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Many numbers in the game and in this almanac are given in ticks or days. The conversions come first, then the durations that come up most often.

li.heading: From ticks to years
li.after: To turn ticks into hours, divide by 2,500; into days, divide by 60,000. Seasons are the easiest unit to plan in: before a winter quadrum starts, have 15 days of food in store.

table.li: Infection roll on a wound | 15,000 to 45,000 ticks (6 to 18 hours) after it can become infected
Seeing a corpse | Half a day
Sleep penalties, eating without a table | 1 day
Random infestations | At most once every 20 days

li.heading: Growing time
li.text: Plants rest from about 19:12 to 6:00 and grow during the other 13.2 hours, so real growth takes about 1.82 times the listed grow days.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: temperatures
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: The temperatures that matter for crops, food, work, comfort, bugs and fire
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Below 0 °C the meat keeps. Below -10 °C most crops start dying.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Temperature decides whether crops grow, whether food rots, how fast people work and whether insects can nest under a mountain. Look up what you're worried about in the table below.

table.li: Crops | Below 0 °C or above 58 °C | Stop growing
Food | 0 °C or below | Stops spoiling, and starts again above it
Passive cooler | 17 °C | The lowest it can bring a room, so it can't keep food
Workbenches | 10-35 °C | Comfortable for many, the electric stove and stonecutter's table among them; 70% speed outside that range
Heat wave | Up to +17 °C | Lasts 1.5-3.5 days
Infestations | Above -17 °C | Possible under overhead mountain; less likely below -8 °C

points.li: Keep the freezer well below 0 °C, for example with coolers set to -5 °C and -10 °C.
Heat workrooms in winter and cool them in summer so benches stay between 10 and 35 °C.
Before a cold snap or the first hard frost, harvest anything at least 65% grown.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: mood and break thresholds
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Break points, expectations, recreation and the everyday thoughts that add up
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A missing table and a cold night already add up to -7 mood.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Mood is the sum of many small thoughts, and the break thresholds decide when a low mood turns into a mental break. The break lines come first, then the everyday thoughts that push colonists toward them or away from them.

li.heading: Break lines

table.li: Break | Possible below | Average time between breaks

li.after: Traits move the minor line, but never below 1% or above 50%. A break is followed by catharsis: +40 per stack, up to 5 stacks (122 at most), for 3 days. Keep everyone well above 35%, so one bad day doesn't push them under the line.

li.heading: Everyday thoughts

table.li: Slept on the ground, outside, in the cold or in the heat | -4 each

li.after: Fix the cheap thoughts first: a table, a bed, a roof and buried bodies are worth 3 to 6 mood each.

li.heading: Wealth, recreation and beauty
li.text:
Expectations follow colony wealth: +30 below 15,000, +24 up to 31,000, +18 up to 81,000, +12 up to 182,000, +6 up to 308,000, and 0 above that. Each step takes 6 mood from everyone, so raise comfort as wealth grows.
Recreation gives +10 at 85-100%, +5 at 70-85%, -5 at 15-30%, -10 below 15% and -20 when it's empty. It falls 2.5% an hour while above 30%.
Surroundings with beauty 6 or more give +15, 4.5 gives +10 and 2.5 gives +5. From -0.5 up to that there's nothing either way; below it the mood turns to -5, then -10, and -15 at -4.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: room stat bands
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Impressiveness, space, cleanliness, beauty and wealth bands, and room roles
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A marble room with blood on the floor still scores as a dirty room.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Every room has four stats that combine into impressiveness, and impressiveness sets the mood bonus for bedrooms, dining rooms and rec rooms. The lowest of the four counts extra, so one weak stat pulls the whole score down.

li.heading: The formula
li.text: Impressiveness = 65 x the average of four factors + 35 x the smallest. The factors are wealth / 1,500, beauty / 3, space / 125, and 1 + cleanliness / 2.5. Check the room's stats and raise the lowest of the four first.

li.heading: The four stats

table.li: Space | Under 12.5 cramped, 12.5 rather tight, 29 average-sized, 55 somewhat spacious, 70 quite spacious, 130 very spacious
Cleanliness | Below -1.1 very dirty, -0.05 to 0.39 clean, 0.4 or more sterile
Beauty | Below -3.5 hideous, below 0 ugly, 0-2.39 neutral, 2.4 pretty, 5 beautiful, 15 very beautiful, 50 extremely beautiful
Wealth | Under 500 impoverished, 700 mediocre, 2,000 somewhat rich, 4,000 rich, 10,000 luxurious, 40,000 very luxurious

li.after: Space is 1.4 per tile, minus 0.9 for each tile furniture blocks, so count it after the furniture goes in: a furnished 5x5 bedroom comes to about 31. Cleanliness is counted per tile too: sterile tile +0.6, filth -5, blood -10, vomit -15.

li.heading: Room roles
li.text:
A room takes whichever role scores highest: prison cell 170,000; barracks 100,100 per bed; bedroom and hospital 100,000; lab 60 per item; kitchen 28 per stove; workshop 27 per bench; dining room 12 per table; rec room 7 per item; storeroom 1 per shelf.
That's why beds stay out of kitchens and workshops: a bed's 100,000 beats any bench and turns the room into a bedroom.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: wealth and raid numbers
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: How your wealth and your people turn into raid points
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Every silver coin in storage counts toward the next raid.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Raid size is priced from your wealth and your people, then scaled by difficulty and by how the colony has been doing. These are the base numbers in recent versions; treat them as close guides, not exact values.

li.heading: How the points add up
li.text:
Raid points = (wealth points + pawn points) x difficulty x starting factor x adaptation, never below 35 or above 10,000.
The wealth counted for raids is items + creatures + half of buildings. It turns into wealth points on a curve: 0 up to 14,000 wealth, 2,400 at 400,000, 3,600 at 700,000 and 4,200 at 1,000,000. Each colonist adds pawn points: 15 up to 10,000 wealth, 140 at 400,000 and 200 at 1,000,000. Slaves count 75% of a colonist, babies 0%, and children from 0% at age 3 to 100% at 18.

li.heading: Difficulty and timing
li.after: The starting factor is 0.7 up to day 10 and 1.0 from day 40. Adaptation starts at 0.8, can reach about 1.47 while things go well, and drops after colonists die.

li.heading: Where the wealth should go
li.text: Items count in full toward raid points and don't help you defend, so sell or use idle silver, gold and art. Spend wealth on defenders and defenses first: they add raid points too, but they also help you fight. Before a big trade or loot haul, work out what it adds to the next raid.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: medicine numbers
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Medicine potency, hospital beds, infection, surgery and disease at a glance
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Glitterworld medicine is 1.6 times as strong as industrial, and much harder to replace.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: The numbers behind tending, infection and surgery. Most of them improve with a skilled doctor, real medicine, and a clean, lit room with a hospital bed.

li.heading: Medicine and beds
li.after: Potency multiplies both tend quality and surgery success. Use industrial medicine for serious wounds and surgery, herbal for the rest, and glitterworld only when conditions are bad. A hospital bed adds +10% tend quality and 1.11x immunity gain; with a vitals monitor, +17% and 1.13x.

li.heading: Infection
li.text:
Each wound has its own chance of infection: 30% for bites and burns, 25% for frostbite, 20% for shredding and 15% for most others. Tending cuts that to between 85% and 5% of it; a clean, floored room halves it and a sterile one takes it to 32%.
An untreated infection grows +0.84 severity a day. Amputate before 90%; past 97% the operation rarely succeeds.

li.heading: Surgery
li.text: Surgery success = surgeon x bed x medicine x operation x inspiration, capped at 98%. Industrial medicine can reach the cap in a good room, so clean the hospital floor and light the beds before any operation.

li.heading: Diseases and addiction
li.after:
Tend infections and diseases about every 12 hours. Gut worms and muscle parasites are cured at 300% total tend quality.
Luciferium always causes addiction and must then be taken every 6 days.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: power numbers
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Generator output, battery storage, reach, and the big power draws
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A battery gives back only half of the power sent into it.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: The figures to check when you plan a power grid: what each generator produces, what batteries hold, how far appliances reach, and which devices draw the most.

li.heading: Generators

table.li: Wood-fired | 1,000 W, burning 22 wood a day
Chemfuel | 1,000 W, burning 4.5 chemfuel a day
Solar | Up to 1,700 W, by day

li.after: Add up your draw and compare it with what you generate at night, not at noon. Use more than one kind of generator, plus a few batteries, so a dark night or a still day doesn't black out the grid. An eclipse lasts 0.75-1.25 days and starves solar panels; a solar flare lasts 0.15-0.5 days and shuts down every powered device.

li.heading: Batteries and wiring
li.text:
A battery stores 600 Wd, charges at 50% efficiency and loses 5 Wd a day. Appliances connect from up to 6 tiles away; conduits, switches, batteries and generators must touch.
Random short circuits have an 8-day cooldown. In recent versions, roofed batteries and hidden conduits prevent them.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: colony numbers
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Work priorities, research costs, prisoners and slaves at a glance
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A prisoner eats from the colony's stores every day it takes to recruit them.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: The quick figures for running the colony day to day: what key research costs, how prisoners are won over and what keeps slaves in line. Work priorities run from 1 (first) to 4 (last), and a blank box means never. The matching Management page says what to do about each number.

li.heading: Research costs
li.after: On a tribal start, read research costs from the research tab: they already include the tribal increase.

li.heading: Prisoners
li.text: Each chat removes 1.0 resistance x warden opinion (50-150%) x prisoner mood (20-150%). Restraints slow a prisoner by 65%. A prison break can spread to rooms within 20 tiles.

li.heading: Slaves (Ideology)
li.after: Slave rebellions have a 45-day base average. They come 5x as often at 0% suppression, 4x with a weapon within 7 tiles, and 20x with no free colonist on the map. Slaves work at 85% speed, and their own expectations give +28 to +46 mood.
